name: 2109 Prairie Avenue — the Robert Roloson house, a stone front under a mansard with a veranda across the front and down the south side

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B brick dwelling with a stone front, wrapped on the north and west by a one-storey frame veranda (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1842 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: T-3666 (piece 2 of T-1924, the S13 package of the T-1837 programme) refines the district draft (T-2352) in place under the same id onto the K01 frontage assembly. What is read: sheet 35 of the 1911 Sanborn for the plan (the front block, the rear block stepping out south, the frame back porch, the frame veranda across the front and down the south side) and the one picture of the house, the Armour photograph (data/sources/chicagology_2115_armour_photo.json), whose left edge catches the front's south bay, its mansard and dormer, the veranda and the rear block's cornice. Everything the picture does not show is reconstructed and says so; liberty L-k01-2109-roloson-3666. Research note: docs/RESEARCH/k01-2109-roloson-3666/README.md.

documented_range.note: The 1911 sheet draws the house and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped); the Armour photograph is undated. Its building date is not read; the register reports its loss in 1933.

position.symbolic_location: 2109 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_2109 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).
position.note: The rear corner of the '3B' main body on its north wall (lot frame u 39.335, v -6.27 from the middle of the rear lot line): the front block's rear line where the rear block steps out south (raster column 960, 15.25 m from the street line) and its north wall (row 1128, 1.30 m inside the parcel's north line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet, which carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of trace on this coarser copy. Rotation 179.312 degrees (the draft's) turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The front block off the 1911 sheet at 0.186 m a pixel: its stone front at raster column 918 (7.44 m from the street line), its north wall at row 1128 and its south wall at row 1169.5 (7.72 m), run back to column 960 (15.25 m from the street line, 7.81 m deep), where the rear block steps out south. The rear block and the frame back porch are K01 rear wings.

stories.note: '3B' printed on the 1911 sheet: three storeys over a basement, which the Armour photograph shows as two storeys of wall under the bracketed cornice and the mansard's attic over them; K01 counts the walls' storeys, the attic is the mansard's (mansard).

construction.note: The sheet colours the street front blue (stone), a band about 1.2 m deep across the whole 7.7 m front, on a pink (brick) house; the census reads it '3B brick dwelling with a stone front'. The photograph's pale front agrees.

principal_floor_m.note: The veranda's floor in the Armour photograph, about 1.7 m over the yard on its open piers (y 1115 against grade at y 1290 px, about 100 px a metre at the veranda's face, scaled by the front's second-storey light, about 1.05 m wide); the principal floor is laid level with it.

storey_heights_m.note: The photograph's two storeys of wall: the principal storey to the veranda's flat roof and a little over it (y 1115-700 px at the veranda's face, about 4.2 m), the second storey to the frieze under the cornice (y 745-420 px on the wall, about 3.8-4.0 m, the round-headed light 2.3 m of it under its keyed hood, which stops just under the frieze).

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A stone front on its brick backing, as every K01 stone front.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: A brick-and-a-half wall, as every K01 brick house.

service_wall_brick.note: The one K03 panel k03_brick lays.

face_brick.note: The flanks and the rear are common brick, which the photograph shows only under the veranda and in shadow: a Chicago common brick, salmon run, as the row's.

stone_front.note: The sheet's stone front; the photograph shows it pale, smooth and uncoursed to the eye at its scale, with no rusticated base above the veranda; the basement behind the open piers, in shadow, is laid on two rusticated courses as the avenue's stone fronts (reconstructed). A smooth Lemont limestone, the avenue's commonest pale stone, is the reconstructed fabric.

street_front_trim.note: K01's flat stone lintel for any flat-headed light; the front's lights are round-headed (street_front_round_heads), so it lays none.

street_front_round_heads.note: The photograph's second-storey light at the front's south end is round-headed under a moulded hood with a carved key (x 55-150, y 455-700 px); the principal storey's light under it, seen through the veranda, rises to a round head too. Both storeys' front lights are laid round-headed and keyed; the north part of the front is out of the frame, so its lights repeat the south one's.

wall_head.note: The photograph's frieze, a band about 0.5 m deep with a long sunk panel and a lozenge (y 380-420 px), under a bracketed cornice whose paired consoles turn the front's south corner (x 190-240, y 360-420 px). K10's bracketed timber cornice over a K01 frieze; the panel's carving is finer than K01 lays.

roof_form.note: The photograph's slated mansard over the front, its steep face carried up from the cornice to a deck with its own cornice (y 140-340 px), a round-headed dormer in it.

roof_pitch_deg.note: The deck's fall, the K05 mansard's own.

eave_overhang_m.note: The cornice box about 0.6 m out from the stone, as the photograph's consoles reach at the corner.

roof_covering.note: The photograph's mansard face is dark slate; the deck behind it is unseen, a painted tin deck as the avenue's mansards.

mansard.note: The photograph's mansard over the front: its face rising about 2.2 m from the cornice to the deck's cornice (y 340-150 px, about 85 px a metre on the front through the solved camera), and in it over the south bay's light a round-headed dormer, its sash about 0.9 m across and 1.5 m high, framed by a carved surround with a scrolled hood (x 15-160, y 160-340 px). The north part of the front is out of the frame: a second dormer over the north bay is reconstructed to balance it (the middle bay's light under the deck has none, as a three-bay front's centre often had not).

rainwater.note: K04 half-round copper gutters along the mansard's eaves and round pipes to splash stones at the rear corner of the north flank; the photograph shows no pipe on the front.

window_kit.note: K06's two-over-two sash for flat-headed lights and its round fanlight sash for round-headed ones.

stair_landing_depth_m.note: The veranda's depth across the front, which the sheet draws 9.5 px (1.8 m) from its edge to the stone front; the landing is the veranda's floor.

stoop_width_m.note: Steps up to the veranda before the door, which no picture shows; 1.5 m.

entrance_bay.note: The door in the front's north bay (K01's south end of the street front is the real north one here, its v axis running south): the photograph's south bay is a light in both storeys, so the door is elsewhere, and the north bay is the draft's and the register's reading of the entrance; reconstructed.

front_bays.note: Three bays across the 7.72 m front: the photograph puts the south bay's light about 1.3 m from the south corner (its centre at x 102 px against the corner at x 225, about 95 px a metre); the north bay mirrors it and the middle bay is centred (reconstructed: out of the frame).

side_bays.note: K01's south wall here is the real north one, beside 2101 across about 1.3 m of side yard (the sheet): two lights a storey on the front block, reconstructed.

north_bays.note: K01's north wall here is the real south one, under the veranda's south run: the photograph shows tall lights in it behind the columns (x 380-470 px), two a storey between the rear block's step and the front corner; places reconstructed.

rear_bays.note: The main body's rear wall stands behind the rear block (rear_wings) across its whole width: no light of its own.

sash_by_storey.note: The photograph's second-storey light about 1.05 m wide and 2.3 m to its round head (x 55-150, y 470-700 px), its sill about 0.6 m over the floor; the principal storey's taller, as the avenue's were and as the veranda shows it rising behind the columns, 3.0 m.

basement_lights.note: Area lights in the basement, behind the veranda's open piers where the photograph is in shadow; reconstructed.

chimneys.note: The photograph's tall stack over the deck behind the south dormer (x 125-165, y 20-150 px), standing about 1.6 m over the deck, on the south wall a few metres back from the front; a second stack on the north wall is reconstructed.

entrance_kit.note: The veranda across the front, which the sheet draws in yellow (frame) 1.8 m deep and the photograph shows on columns about 0.28 m through, under a deep plain entablature (beam 0.6 m) and an almost flat roof (y 700-745 px), its balustrade of turned balusters between pedestals and its floor on open piers. The door behind it and the steps up to it are out of the frame: a panelled door in the north bay under the veranda, reconstructed; the posts at the front's corners and between the bays.

side_porch.note: The veranda's run down the south side, which the sheet draws 2.7 m deep (14.5 px) from the front back to where the rear block steps out south, and the photograph shows on round columns receding along it (x 520, 460, 400, 340 px), paired at the corner on pedestals, under the same deep entablature. K01's side porch carries a low balustrade on its roof that the photograph does not show (liberty).

rear_wings.note: The sheet's plan behind the front block (0.186 m a pixel): the brick body steps out 2.32 m south of the front block 15.25 m from the street line (column 960), where the veranda's south run ends, and runs back to 25.1 m (column 1013); its north-east corner, 20.5-26.4 m from the street line and 2.43 m in from the north wall, is a yellow (frame) part, a back porch. The rear block stands at the front's height under the '3B', as the photograph shows its cornice beyond the veranda at the step's south-west corner (x 225-285, y 515-540 px): on K01's rear wings, the first running past the main body's south end (past_host) with a front of its own there, under a flat deck behind a timber cornice (reconstructed). The back porch is one storey (reconstructed).

boundary.note: The photograph's low stone curb along the walk before 2109 (x 0-670, y 1250-1300 px), about 0.3 m high, with no fence on it; its opening for the walk to the steps is out of the frame, before the door (reconstructed).

yard.note: The front yard's condition in 1904 as K14 lays the avenue's: a flagged walk to the steps, earth under the veranda.
